title: What is known about 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_0RE---_1LF1LA_1LA1LF.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is always blocks 1k 0 separated by single zeros, and the machine halts exactly if B meets 0 0 1: a double zero inside the tape (proved shape: Lean). In 109 steps B met a 0 followed by another 0 only at the blank right end of the tape. Whether a double zero can ever form is a question about a chaotic, cellular-automaton-like evolution.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: B with 0 under the head, 0 right, 1 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 66,036 cells have been visited and 52,367 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.083).

claims.title: The sweeps' shift rules
claims.text: B runs right over 1s and F runs left over 1s; moving left, E (through A) turns each pair 11 into 01; moving right, A (through B and C) turns each 0101 into 1110. Each holds for every n and every surrounding tape.

claims.title: The shape of a halt
claims.text: From B> 0 0 1 the machine reaches D on a 1 in 2 steps and halts on the next. Conversely (by reading the table, not formalized) D is entered only from C on a 0 and C only from B on a 0, so every halt comes this way.

claims.title: No double zero inside the tape so far
claims.text: In the first 109 steps B reads a 0 about 6.2·107 times; the next cell is a 0 only 42 times, all at the blank right end (then D reads a blank 0 and moves on). C reads a 0 only those 42 times. The closest calls: B> 0 1 0 0, 6 times.

claims.title: Sweeps and a frozen right part
claims.text: Sampled each time the head is in A at the left end, the tape is a list of blocks 1<sup>k</sup> 0 with odd k. The left part (k = 1 mod 4 only) is rewritten at every sweep; the right part (k = 1 or 3 mod 4) stays frozen between rare deep sweeps that reach the right end, at steps 1.9·10<sup>6</sup>, 6.4·10<sup>6</sup>, 1.9·10<sup>7</sup>, 6.1·10<sup>7</sup>, 1.9·10<sup>8</sup>, 5.8·10<sup>8</sup> (about 3.1 times apart: the logarithmic right side). How deep a sweep reaches varies like the carries of a counter, which draws the triangles of the space-time diagram.

claims.title: No closed tape language from short windows
claims.text: bbtools.ctl with windows of K = 2 to 6 cells closes but allows halts (D reading 1); the right automaton doubles with K, so the right side is not regular at this scale. n-gram CPS (widths 3 to 7, with history and LRU) also fails.
claims.where: tools/py/bbtools/ctl.py; tools/c/ngramcps.c (run for the G02 group, not stored here)

claims.title: Same tapes as 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA
claims.text: At each of the 42 events C on a 0 at the right end in its first 5.9·10<sup>8</sup> steps, the tape is identical to the tape of 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA at its own 42 such events, which come 1.5 times later in steps. The correspondence is observed, not proved.
claims.where: c/tok.c (./tok M 1000000000 C 0 R 0 1000 0 for both machines)

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 24, history 1 up to width 24, history 2 up to width 24, history 3 up to width 24, LRU history up to width 4 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 20, p = 3 up to width 20, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..8; n = 9 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly if a double zero (followed by a 1) forms inside the tape and B reaches it. The local rules keep zeros single in every case seen, but the evolution looks chaotic, and no invariant explaining it is known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 66,036 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
Sweeps rewrite the tape like a cellular automaton; zeros stay single.

sections.eyebrow: What the tape is made of
sections.heading: Blocks of ones, single zeros
html: Stop the machine whenever the head is in state A at the left end of the tape. The tape is then always a list of blocks 1k 0: runs of ones separated by single zeros, with k odd. Here it is at step 100,542 (each block written as its k):

The left part has only k = 1, 5, 9, 13, ... (1 more than a multiple of 4); further right also 3, 7, 15, ... appear. At the next samples (steps 100,894 and onwards) the first forty-odd blocks are different and the rest is identical: each sweep rewrites the left part and turns back before the right part.

sections.heading: A cellular automaton drawn by a bouncer
html: The head bounces. Moving left, F runs over ones; at a zero it fills it in and A and E then turn pairs 11 into 01 until they meet another zero. Moving right, B runs over ones and A, B, C turn 0101 into 1110. Each sweep thus rewrites every block from its neighbours, like one time step of a cellular automaton, and the space-time diagram above shows the typical nested triangles of such automata.

How far right a sweep goes before turning varies like the carries of a counter: most sweeps stay in the left part, and only rarely (at steps about 3.1 times apart: 6.1·107, 1.9·108, 5.8·108) does one reach the right end and add a cell there. That is the logarithmic side. The left end gains a cell every few sweeps: the square-root side.

sections.heading: Halting needs a double zero
html: The halting transition is D reading a 1, and D is entered only from C reading a 0, which is entered only from B reading a 0. So the machine halts exactly when B, moving right, meets 0 0 1: two zeros side by side with a 1 after them. Lean checks that B> 0 0 1 halts three steps later.

On the samples every zero is single, and in the first 109 steps B met a double zero only 42 times, all at the blank right end, where the cell after them is blank too. Proving that zeros stay single forever would prove that the machine never halts, but the rewriting is chaotic: short-window invariants (closed tape languages up to 6 cells, n-gram CPS up to 7) find nothing.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.504). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.083).
After 109 steps the tape spans 66,036 cells (44,220 left of the start, 143 right), with a density of 1s of 0.793.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB1RA_1LC0RF_1LD1LC_1LE0LB_0LF---_1RA1RB: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→F, F→A and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state F, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RE_0RC---_1LD1LE_1LE1LD_1RF0LC_1RA1RF: rename A→E, B→F, C→A, D→B, E→C, F→D; it is this table started in state C
  • 1RB1RC_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_0LA---: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→F, E→A, F→B and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state E, in a mirror

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA: 4,986,200 configurations, the last at step 6,657,506 here and step 10,000,000 there

summary: A bouncer whose sweeps rewrite a tape of blocks 1^k 0 (always single 0s) like a cellular automaton: the space-time diagram fills with Sierpinski-like triangles; it halts only if a double 0 ever forms inside the tape.
